title: How overlapping windows move
notes: Each new forecast uses actual readings available at its forecast time. Earlier target readings can appear as inputs later. Windows in a batch remain independent. Randomly splitting overlapping targets across train and test could leak answers.

notes: The dataset uses target start indices to slice the original array on demand. The DataLoader groups examples, keeping inputs, targets and masks aligned. Four is the number of forecast windows in a batch.

title: Normalization: a numerical example
notes: These numbers are illustrative. The normalized value of 2 means the reading is two training standard deviations above the training mean. A raw value of 80 normalizes to minus one. All splits use the same training statistics.

title: Masking and sensor coverage
items:
696 scored sensors
20 have no eligible test targets
notes: The zero mask is applied to actual future targets, not to model predictions. A model prediction of zero is still scored when the actual target is nonzero. Zeros may represent true zero flow or missing values.

title: MAE, RMSE and MAPE by example
notes: MAE averages absolute errors in the flow units. RMSE squares errors before averaging, so larger errors have greater influence. MAPE divides the absolute error by each nonzero actual target before averaging.

title: The LSTM state across time
items:
Read traffic at t₁
Update hidden and cell states

Read traffic at t₂
Use states from step 1

Read last observation
Keep final hidden state
notes: For one sensor, the LSTM reads 12 values in order. The cell state carries information along the sequence. Gates regulate what is retained, added and exposed. Each window and sensor sequence begins with fresh states.

title: One shared LSTM for 716 sensors
items:
Same LSTM weights
fresh states per sequence
notes: The project does not train 716 separate LSTMs. Each sensor history passes through the same learned model. Within this model, one sensor’s current readings do not enter another sensor’s sequence.

title: How a linear layer predicts 12 values
items:
Final hidden state
32 values for small LSTM

32 weights + one bias
combine all 32 values

12 sets of weights
produce 12 forecast steps
notes: For each forecast time, a linear layer multiplies each of the 32 hidden values by its learned weight and sums them with a bias. The 12 outputs are generated together. The contextual LSTM uses 256 hidden values at its selected width.

title: Contextual LSTM: how 41 is formed
notes: At one sensor and one historical time step, the model concatenates 1 plus 16 plus 8 plus 16 values. For 12 past steps, one sensor has shape 12 by 41. Sensor identity is learned context and supplies no other sensor’s current traffic readings.

title: LSTM tensor shapes through the model
notes: The axes are permuted so each sensor in each window is a separate sequence. The batch and sensor axes are combined, the two LSTM layers process each sequence, and the head produces 12 future values. The model restores time and sensor axes.

title: How we count trainable parameters
notes: A trainable parameter is one learned weight or bias. Count the elements in all trainable tensors and add them. The 256-unit LSTM’s two recurrent layers have 306,176 and 526,336 parameters. Fixed gather and restore indices are buffers, not trainable parameters.

title: PatchSTG: project one sensor history
items:
12 time steps × 3 values
traffic, slot and weekday

36 inputs → 64 outputs
learned weights and biases
notes: The temporal convolution uses all three channels and 12 historical positions. It creates 64 values per sensor. The model concatenates time-slot and weekday embeddings for the last historical step and a sensor embedding to obtain a 192-value vector.

title: From one sensor to Query, Key and Value
items:
192 inputs → 576 outputs
learned weights and biases
notes: A single learned linear layer creates all three vectors together. Each of its 576 output numbers is a weighted sum of the 192 input values plus a bias. Splitting the output gives one query, key and value vector of width 192.

title: One query scores 64 keys
notes: The query at one position is compared with every key in its patch, including its own. Each score is a dot product. With all 64 queries, the scores form a 64 by 64 matrix. Each row is one query’s scores.

title: Scaling and softmax: numerical example
items:
Weights ≈ 0.33 and 0.67
The two weights sum to 1
notes: This is a two-dimensional teaching example. Actual queries and keys have width 192 and are divided by the square root of 192. Softmax is applied across the keys for each query, turning its scores into attention weights.

title: Where the Value vectors are added
notes: Each query has its own set of weights. For one query, multiply every Value vector by its corresponding weight and add down each feature column. One query gives one 192-value result. The 64 queries therefore give 64 such results.

title: Inside one PatchSTG block
items:
Attention over 64 positions
within each patch

Normalize, attend, add
normalize, feed forward, add

Attention over 16 patches
at the same position
notes: Each attention stage uses normalization, attention with a residual addition, then a feed-forward network with another residual addition. Depth occurs before breadth. A position can therefore carry information gathered from its patch into the breadth stage. The block is repeated five times with separate learned parameters.

title: Restore original sensor order
items:
One saved position
for each original sensor
notes: The map is constructed before attention and records the designated original position for each sensor. After the fifth block, the model gathers those 716 positions in original sensor order. It does not average all repeated positions. The shared forecast head converts each 192-value representation to 12 normalized predictions.

title: Best checkpoint and latest checkpoint
items:
Lowest validation MAE
used for evaluation

Latest weights + Adam state
used to resume training
notes: Best and latest checkpoints answer different needs. If training stops after epoch 40 with the best validation score at epoch 37, resume from the latest state but evaluate the validation-selected weights from epoch 37.

title: Interpreting the error graphs
items:
Each point pools a single lead
15 to 180 minutes ahead

Histogram of LSTM sensor MAEs
696 sensors with valid targets

Pools all eligible forecast–target
pairs across sensors and leads
notes: The forecast-distance plot reveals how accuracy changes with the prediction horizon. The sensor histogram shows variation for the selected LSTM only. Overall pooled MAE weights each included forecast-target pair equally, so it is not generally the simple average of per-sensor MAEs.

title: GPU checks and numerical precision
items:
Move model and batch tensors
to compatible devices

Compare isolated and batched
inputs and outputs

Warm up and synchronize
measure the defined scope
notes: The contextual probe checks the recurrent inputs exactly and compares outputs within tolerance. Floating point calculations can differ slightly across execution layouts. An early 256-width probe failed and the revised explicit FP32 check passed. A warmed repeated-batch timing omits other full-epoch work.
